title: More Materials. Smarter Workflows. What’s New for FDM 3D Printing in H2 2026
summary: Explore the latest Stratasys FDM 3D printing updates for H2 2026, including new materials, larger-format capabilities, composite printing and smarter workflows.
body_markdown:
### **Push Performance: Bringing High-Performance Materials to More Platforms**


Material expansion continues across the FDM portfolio, beginning with the addition of[Antero® 800NA CG](https://www.stratasys.com/en/materials/materials-catalog/fdm-materials/antero-800na/) to the F3300. This high-performance PEKK-based thermoplastic combines demanding mechanical and thermal properties with the throughput and production economics of the F3300, enabling manufacturers to pursue advanced aerospace, space, and harsh-environment applications at production scale.


The F3300 material portfolio is also expanding with[ABS-ESD7™](https://www.stratasys.com/en/materials/materials-catalog/fdm-materials/abs-esd7/) , a static-dissipative thermoplastic designed to help protect sensitive electronic components. By pairing proven ESD performance with the speed and productivity of the F3300, manufacturers can produce enclosures, jigs, fixtures, test devices, and functional components while minimizing risks associated with electrostatic discharge.


For customers seeking high-temperature performance,[ULTEM™ 1010](https://www.stratasys.com/en/materials/materials-catalog/fdm-materials/ultem-1010/) resin was announced for the F3300, earlier this year. With the highest temperature rating and lowest coefficient of thermal expansion of any FDM material on the platform, it supports precise composite layup tools, high-temperature fixtures, and demanding prototypes. Customers using the F900® and Fortus® 450mc can also access ULTEM 1010 resin in large-capacity spools through the Fortus FDC™, supporting longer uninterrupted print times, integrated material drying, and improved part consistency.
